title: chrootarchive: close root fd before chroot(".") in untar()
body:
untar() keeps the inherited root fd open across chroot("."), which fails with EPERM on FreeBSD when the process holds an open directory fd and its root is not the system root (e.g., in a jail, under the default kern.chroot_allow_open_directories=1):

  `unpacking failed (error: exit status 1; output: chroot ".": operation not permitted)`

With vfs, this breaks creating a layer from a parent, preventing podman and buildah from building or running inside a FreeBSD container.

Close the fd right after fchdir(). cwd still holds the directory reference so chroot(".") is unchanged, and on Linux the fd just closes a few lines earlier.
